speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the neck swelling you have noticed, including how long it has been there, its size, and whether it is painful or moves when you swallow.

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Thyroid (likely Anaplastic or Metastatic from a previous primary) or Metastasis from Colon Cancer.

Given the patient's history of colon cancer and current neck swelling, I need to know if the swelling is hard/fixed or soft/movable, and whether he has experienced any weight loss or hoarseness recently. Can you describe the texture of the lump and any changes in your voice or difficulty swallowing?
